Prevention: Follow recommended orchard management practices (regular pruning, optimum manuring, and fertilization, etc.)
Bag fruits using wax paper or oiled newspaper to prevent egg laying in fruits after flower petals drop following fertilization.
Collect infested dropped fruits and bury inside soil at depth of at least 35cm from soil surface.
Follow quarantine measures strictly (don't carry infected citrus fruits) to prevent entry and spread of pest in a new area.
Monitoring: This uni-voltine (one generation per year) species of fruit fly attacks fruits of a wide range of
Citrus spp. fruits such as sweet orange, lemon, and mandarin etc.
Monitor citrus orchard using protein bait trap (1 trap/ha).
Take action when 4-6 adult flies are detected in the trap. 1 cm long brownish body with three yellow markings on thorax. 1cm wings with dark band along the margin of front wing.
Check for egg-laid puncture sites on the fruit-rind.
Collect the fallen fruit and observe maggots inside the cut-opened fruit.
Infected fruits are lighter and have holes in the outer surface of rind of the fruit.
Observe the field life history of the pest in the orchard to apply prevention measures.
If there is fruit infestation by maggots, apply preventive measures for next year.
Direct Control: Collect & bury infested and dropped fruits at least 35cm deep in soil every 7 days, feed to livestock, use for biogas pit, or kill in sealed plastic bag by exposing to the sun to break the life cycle of fruit fly.
The maggots of fruit fly pupate in the soil; tillage the soil under the tree canopies to kill larvae and/or pupae resting in the soil.
Tree canopy soil treatment with crushed neem seed cake @ 50-60 kg/ha after fruit harvest (Jan-Feb).
Azadirachtin (a botanical product) (@ 3 ml/litre water) in the orchard during
May-July in 15 day intervals to deter egg laying.
Metarhizium anisopliae @ 2-3 kg/ha against larvae; incorporate this bio- pesticide in soil at the time of peak fruit maturing period (Jan-Feb).

Restrictions: Apply recommended insecticides alternatively to prevent resistance.
